newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt money markets tight, await bond allocations.
newsitem.headline: Egypt money markets tight, await bond allocations.

text.p: The short-term Egyptian pound money market saw little dealing on Monday as bankers waited to see what their allocations would be in the treasury's new seven-year bonds, the bankers said.

Bankers quoted overnight rates at 10 3/8 to 10 1/2 percent in minimal business, against between 10 to 10 5/8 percent on Sunday. One banker said he had heard one-week done at 10 3/4 but others said there was no one-week dealing.
"Banks are holding on to what they have, because of the treasury bonds. Even the public-sector banks are not lending for the moment," one banker said.

The Central Bank is offering bonds worth four billion pounds at a fixed rate of 11 percent. Monday is the last day for applications and a Central Bank official said the results of the offer would be available on Tuesday.
There was little apparent interest in the central bank's offer to repurchase treasury bills worth 500 million pounds for two weeks starting on Tuesday.
